title: Host a backend on Cloud Run

prerequisites.label: A GCP project is selected
prerequisites.hint: Check the project picker in the console top bar.

prerequisites.label: Billing is enabled on the project
prerequisites.hint: Cloud Run needs a billing account even for free-tier use.

prerequisites.label: The Cloud Console is open in this window
Console language is English
prerequisites.hint: Baymax finds buttons by their English names.

nextSteps: This deployed Google's sample container — swap in your own image URL when you're ready.
A real backend needs its container port and env vars set (Edit & deploy new revision).
Check scaling: max instances caps your cost, min 0 means scale-to-zero.
Your service URL is public — restrict access if it shouldn't be.

steps.title: Search for Cloud Run
steps.description: Click the search bar at the top of the console and type "Cloud Run". You can find any GCP product this way.
steps.selector: input.pcc-search-input, input[placeholder*="Search" i], input[aria-label*="search for resources" i]
steps.revealSelector: input.pcc-search-input, input[placeholder*="Search" i], input[aria-label*="search for resources" i], button[aria-label="Open search" i]
steps.fallbackHint: I can't find the search bar — the Console hides it behind a 🔍 icon when its window gets narrow. Drag my edge to give the Console more room and I'll spot it, or let me take you straight to Cloud Run.

steps.title: Open Cloud Run from the results
steps.description: Click the "Cloud Run" result (the Product) to open the Cloud Run page.
steps.name: Cloud Run
steps.revealSelector: input.pcc-search-input, input[placeholder*="Search" i], input[aria-label*="search for resources" i], button[aria-label="Open search" i]
steps.fallbackHint: I can't find the "Cloud Run" result — the suggestions list closes as soon as the Console loses focus, and a narrow window hides the search bar behind a 🔍 icon. Try the search again, or let me take you straight to Cloud Run.

steps.title: Deploy a container
steps.description: You're in Cloud Run now. Click "Deploy container" to create a new service from a container image.
steps.name: Deploy container

steps.title: Use the sample container
steps.description: Click "Test with a sample container" — it fills in Google's demo image so you can try the flow. (Deploying your own app instead? Paste your image URL into the Container image URL field.)
steps.name: Test with a sample container

steps.title: Name your service
steps.description: The service name auto-filled as "hello" from the sample image. Keep it, or type a name you like — this becomes part of your service URL and can't be changed later.
steps.name: Service name

steps.title: Choose a region
steps.description: Pick where your service runs. The default works fine — asia-southeast1 (Singapore) is closest if you're in Southeast Asia. This also can't be changed later.
steps.name: Region

steps.title: Allow public access
steps.description: Under Authentication, choose "Allow public access" so your service gets a URL anyone can open in a browser. (For internal APIs you'd require authentication instead.)
steps.name: Allow public access

steps.title: Create the service
steps.description: Click "Create" to deploy. If a red error points at the Security section, open it and set Service account to "Default compute service account", then click Create again.
steps.name: Create

steps.title: Watch it go live
steps.description: Cloud Run is provisioning your service — wait for the green check next to the service name (under a minute). Then click the URL to see your app live!
